title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & cost breakdown - Stellar Retail
summary: Redwood AE/SE walked Stellar through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and the cost breakdown features. Customer asked about tenant isolation, VPC/private deployment options, and how routing + batching influence per-route cost. Agreed to run a short benchmark with their sample prompts and share security docs + provisional pricing.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood. With me is Priya our SE and Carlos from customer success. Quick intro?
[00:12] Maya Chen: Hi Maya here, Head of Data at Stellar Retail. Liam and Rita and Samir on the call as well.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Great, the goal today is a quick console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdown that you asked about. We'll demo live, stop for questions.
[00:34] Priya Shah: I'll share my screen, hop in. (screen share sound) Okay, you should see the Redwood Console homepage, note this is a staging tenant for the demo so numbers are synthetic.
[00:47] Priya Shah: First page is the global usage view — overall tokens, embedding units, requests per minute. You can filter by model, by route, and by time window.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Quick question — can filters be scoped to org/team so our product teams only see their routes?
[01:12] Priya Shah: Yes, RBAC supports per-team views and you can pin dashboards to a team. We also integrate with SSO/SAML so your identity provider maps groups to Redwood roles.
[01:24] Maya Chen: And audit logs for who downloaded usage?
[01:28] Carlos Mendez: Yep, audit logs plus exportable CSVs; retention depends on plan, but we can enable longer retention for Dedicated/Private.
[01:36] Priya Shah: Jumping into per-route dashboards — here's a route called "product-search-autocomplete". It shows latency p50/p95, tokens per request distribution, cost per 1k requests, and error rates.
[01:52] Priya Shah: Notice the token-level cost waterfall — model compute, KV cache hits (shows savings), batching efficiency, and network egress.
[02:05] Samir Patel: That KV cache line, is that prefix cache or full KV cache for generation? We are worried about cold-start token costs.
[02:14] Priya Shah: Good callout. This shows KV cache (key-value cache) hit rates for autoregressive workloads; you can enable prefix caching for common prompts which reduces token spend. Cold-starts show higher cost — console highlights those and suggests cacheable prefixes.
[02:30] Jordan Lee: Also, Optimize can suggest batching window changes and quantization profiles per route to hit cost targets. We'll show a sample recommendation later.
[02:42] Maya Chen: From a procurement lens — can you show a concrete cost breakdown for our chat route vs product-search route?
[02:50] Priya Shah: Sure — here's a side-by-side: chat uses a larger model with higher per-token compute; product-search uses a smaller model and benefits more from prefix caching. The console calculates effective cost per end-user interaction after batching and cache savings.
[03:12] Priya Shah: Note the pie chart — 62% model compute, 18% KV cache savings, 10% batching efficiency, 10% misc like network and storage.
[03:24] Rita Gomez: Are these numbers realtime? We need accurate invoices for finance.
[03:29] Carlos Mendez: Cost estimates are near-realtime within a few minutes and we have a billing export you can ingest into your FinOps systems. For Dedicated we can align invoice cadence to commits.
[03:42] Liam O'Connor: Let's talk architecture constraints — we have internal policy that PII cannot leave our VPC. How would Redwood handle that?
[03:51] Jordan Lee: For that use-case we recommend Redwood Private (VPC-onprem option) which runs a customer-managed control plane. You keep data inside your network; we provide a private agent and KMS integration.
[04:07] Priya Shah: Also for hosted with strict residency we offer an encrypted-in-transit and at-rest flow with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and field-level redaction. But Private is the stronger compliance posture.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Does Private mean we need to provide GPUs and maintain them?
[04:24] Priya Shah: There are two flavors — VPC-hosted where Redwood manages the GPUs inside your cloud account (we orchestrate but resources live in your cloud) or full on-prem where you manage hardware. Both integrations support SOC2/ISO checklists and audit logs.
[04:40] Samir Patel: How easy is failover between regions? We need multi-region failover for peak seasons.
[04:46] Jordan Lee: Smart routing supports multi-region policies and automatic fallback to compatible model variants — you can set policies by latency, cost, or region. The console will surface fallback events in the trace logs.
[05:00] Priya Shah: Switching back to the cost page — you can drill into a single route and see example traces that contributed most tokens. It even surface prompt families that have the highest token spend.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Those prompt families — can we set automated alerts if a route exceeds token budget or if regression in quality after quantization?
[05:23] Priya Shah: Yes, Quality monitoring ties to evals; you can set SLAs and regression alerts tied to a prompt set. Optimize also simulates QoE changes under quantization profiles.
[05:36] Liam O'Connor: Objection from our infra team — we've already invested in an in-house GPU cluster. Why not just serve ourselves?
[05:45] Jordan Lee: Totally fair. Typical tradeoffs — you control everything in-house but you absorb ops and model-ops cost and slower kernel/optimizer improvements. Redwood's value is unified runtime, continuous batching, and ongoing kernel/compilation improvements that typically reduce per-token cost. We can run a benchmark to compare run rates on a per-route basis.
[06:05] Priya Shah: And we can demonstrate improvements like kernel selection for longer sequences which your in-house stack may not currently optimize.
[06:15] Maya Chen: Ok, let's talk pilots.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: We usually do a two-week pilot with sample prompts and a couple routes. SE will help you configure routes, caching rules, and suggested batching windows. We run a cost/latency comparison and then share a spreadsheet with estimated monthly run-rate and a suggested Dedicated configuration if you want committed capacity.
[06:33] Priya Shah: I'm going to click into "Recommendations" — here's an Optimize suggestion: reduce chat batching window from 80ms to 40ms during non-peak to improve latency and keep cost within target.
[06:48] Priya Shah: It also suggests quantizing the search model to int8: near-zero latency impact on shorter queries with ~25% cost reduction.
[06:58] Samir Patel: We are nervous about quality loss from quantization, do you have A/B test support?
[07:03] Priya Shah: Absolutely — rollouts support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback. You can tie regressions to eval prompt sets and auto-roll back.
[07:14] Rita Gomez: On procurement — what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated, and can you show provisional pricing?
[07:21] Jordan Lee: Typical reserved commit is monthly or annual; we'll send provisional pricing. For the demo tenant I'm showing an example pricing sheet link here: https://redwood.example/pricing/stellar-proposal (note: demo link).
[07:36] Maya Chen: We also need security docs and SOC2 report.
[07:40] Carlos Mendez: We'll share the security pack (SOC2, ISO docs, penetration test summary, SAML integration guide) right after the call.
[07:48] Priya Shah: Back to the trace view — here's a per-request breakdown: token counts by input vs generated, KV cache hit boolean, batching delta, model variant used and fallback events.
[08:05] Liam O'Connor: Can we export traces to our SIEM?
[08:09] Priya Shah: Yes, we support forwarding logs to common SIEMs and cloud logging sinks. You can also download JSON traces.
[08:18] Maya Chen: Any limitations for healthcare data? We are not PHI-first but some of our partners handle PHI.
[08:26] Jordan Lee: For PHI you almost certainly want Private on-prem or VPC-hosted with strict KMS and field-level redaction; we have customers in regulated health using Private with audit hooks. We'll include case studies.
[08:38] Samir Patel: Can you show an example of the billing export?
[08:42] Priya Shah: Sure (exports CSV) — columns: route_id, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hits, batching_factor, effective_cost_usd. You can map route_id to product teams in the export.
[08:58] Maya Chen: That helps finance to allocate spend.
[09:01] Priya Shah: One more thing — the console has a "what-if" cost simulator: change batching, model, and cache settings and it will project monthly spend based on historical traffic.
[09:14] Jordan Lee: Let's do a quick live what-if for your product-search route — switch model from rwd-search-7b to rwd-search-3b and enable prefix caching; you'll see estimated monthly saving of ~32% and p95 latency increase of 12ms.
[09:33] Liam O'Connor: Hmm that might be acceptable. We'll want to QA on sample queries.
[09:37] Priya Shah: Totally, SE will help set up a validation harness.
[09:41] Rita Gomez: Regarding contracting timeline — we want a month to evaluate and then decide on Dedicated by June.
[09:48] Jordan Lee: Sounds reasonable. We'll propose a pilot window and provisional Dedicated sizing in the proposal.
[09:55] Carlos Mendez: I'll also add success criteria: latency under 200ms p95 for search and cost per search under $0.002, is that roughly what you have in mind?
[10:07] Maya Chen: Yes, those are close — might be tighter for peak events.
[10:11] Jordan Lee: Great, final bits — we captured a few action items, and we'll send the security pack, demo tenant link, and a pricing sheet. Anything else before we wrap?
[10:22] Maya Chen: Please include sample benchmarking steps and required logs we should provide.
[10:28] Priya Shah: We'll include a short doc with data collection template and tarball of sample prompt sets.
[10:34] Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule a pilot kickoff.
[10:40] (call ends)
